messages:
sara: Heads up — during a routine audit we discovered multiple third-party webhook secrets stored in plaintext across infra and integration configs. Need org-wide remediation: rotate/revoke affected secrets, apply short-lived tokens or HMAC verification, and put a temporary limited-access window on endpoints. Full ask below.

james: Scope? which repos/services are affected?

sara: Initial scan found ~8 unique webhook tokens across 5 repos: infra-config, integrations-ci, support-ops, partner-oncall, metrics-sync. Vendors impacted: OpsNotify, PagerTeam, Sentry-inbound (examples). I'll attach per-repo list in the ticket.

elaine: Immediate rotation or staged? We have external partners that need coordinated change windows.

sara: For tokens that are publicly exposed or shared in open channels: immediate revoke. For others: 48h rotation window. Require partners to support either short-lived tokens or HMAC header verification. Also enforce a temporary access window 09:00-18:00 UTC for webhook endpoints until rotation complete.

mike: I'll open the INC and start rotations for infra-config + integrations-ci. @sara can you confirm the exact grep command to locate these?

sara: Use this quick check in each repo:
```
git grep -nE 'webhook|hook_url|secret=|x-hub-signature' -- '*.tf' '*.yaml' '*.yml' '*.env' || true
```
Also scan deployment artifacts and image envs for injected vars.

sec-bot: sec-bot: Created INC-4657 in SecurityOps. Remediation checklist assigned to @mike, @elaine, @james. Due: 48 hours. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4657

james: :thumbsup: I'll coordinate partner notifications. Do we have a partner migration guide?

sara: Draft guide at /docs/security/webhooks-rotation.md. Needs HMAC example — recommend X-Signature (sha256) with timestamp to avoid replay.

elaine: Partner asks for a maintenance window. Proposing Tue 14:00 UTC — aligns with APAC and EMEA.

mike: Rotation plan I'll execute: 1) provision new token in Secret Manager 2) deploy consumer behind feature flag 3) switch traffic to new token 4) revoke old token and remove from repo. Will PR changes and add health-checks.

james: Do we block existing tokens immediately or wait for partner coordination?

sara: Block only tokens explicitly confirmed as leaked or public. For others, follow the 48h schedule. Meanwhile enable rate limits + IP allowlist for webhook endpoints as temporary mitigation (example CIDRs listed in the ticket).

elaine: Note — support-ops webhook for PagerTeam doesn't support short-lived tokens. We'll need to proxy through an internal gateway that signs outbound requests.

mike: I can stand up a lightweight proxy (NGINX auth_request or small lambda) to sign/forward requests. Will include as fallback.

sec-bot: Tip: to scan history use trufflehog or our internal secret scanner, e.g. `trufflehog --regex --entropy=False --rules webhooks.json https://github.com/redwood/repo.git` and also run `git log -p --all | grep -i webhook` for quick checks.

sara: Action owners: @mike — infra-config & integrations-ci, @elaine — support-ops & partner coordination, @james — partner comms. I'll publish an executive summary by EOD and update the INC.

james: Ack. I'll ping partners and update the ticket with proposed maintenance window.

sara: After rotations complete, enforce new policy: no persistent webhook secrets committed to repos. Mandate Secret Manager+OIDC for service accounts and add a CI pre-commit check to block common webhook patterns.

mike: Understood. I'll add the CI check to the integrations pipeline and PR the policy doc.

elaine: Thanks — we'll keep partners in the loop and minimize downtime.

sara: Thanks everyone. If you spot a token during your scan, tag INC-4657 and DM me immediately. :lock:
